full_text:
Ukraine is preparing amendments to the rules governing the operation of businesses during a yellow-level air quality alert. On 18 November, the Verkhovna Rada Committee on Economic Development unanimously supported draft resolution No. 16207, which provides for the abolition of the mandatory closure of businesses without designated shelters. The initiative is intended to reduce the financial burden on small businesses and allow entrepreneurs to determine their own operating arrangements.
Key points at a glance:
- The Verkhovna Rada’s Economic Committee unanimously endorsed draft resolution No. 16207.
- Businesses are being offered the option to decide for themselves whether to operate during a yellow alert.
- Employees will be able to stop work and take shelter at any time.
- The bill is expected to be considered by the Verkhovna Rada during the next plenary week.
What will change for business owners during an air raid alert?
The draft resolution, tabled on 2 November at the initiative of 31 Members of Parliament, provides for a review of the government’s decision No. 1092 of 4 September 2026.
Previously installed requirements for shelters have created serious difficulties for business owners who are unable to install protective structures on their premises.
Under the proposed changes, shops, restaurants, cafés, beauty salons and other businesses will be able to continue operating during a yellow alert level, even if they do not have a designated shelter. A mandatory requirement will be the voluntary, individual, written consent of employees who have decided to remain at their place of work.
Employees will retain the right to take shelter
Every employee will have the right to stop work and seek shelter of their own accord, regardless of any prior written consent. Employers will also be required to inform staff and visitors of any air threat in a timely manner and to comply with the safety measures laid down by law.
The proposed relaxations apply exclusively to the yellow alert level. The document does not alter the rules regarding the mandatory suspension of work during a red alert.
When might the new rules come into force?
According to the MP Yaroslav Zheleznyak, the resolution is due to be put to a vote in the Verkhovna Rada as early as next plenary week.
At the same time, MPs are calling on the Cabinet of Ministers to review the current restrictions without waiting for a decision from the Verkhovna Rada. Should the document be adopted, the government will be advised to make the necessary amendments within three calendar days.
As of 18 November, the new rules had not yet come into force.
